holidays.name: Put a Pillow on Your Fridge Day
holidays.description: A cheeky observance that asks you to set a pillow on top of your refrigerator, mostly so you can enjoy the absurdity of it. Nobody can quite explain what the pillow is for, and that is the whole point.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, internet-era novelty day with no clear founder. It spread through quirky holiday calendars and social media lists.
holidays.funFact: Many novelty-day calendars list it, but no one has ever produced a credible reason for the pillow, which makes it one of the most delightfully pointless holidays around.

holidays.name: National Biscuit Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate fluffy, buttery American-style biscuits, whether you slather them in gravy, honey, jam, or fried chicken.
holidays.origin: It is an unofficial food holiday popular in the United States, especially in the South where biscuits are a cultural staple.
holidays.funFact: The word biscuit comes from the Latin 'bis coctus', meaning 'twice baked', yet a real American biscuit is baked only once.

holidays.name: Learn About Composting Day
holidays.description: A day for turning banana peels and eggshells into garden gold. It encourages people to explore the stinky but rewarding science of compost.
holidays.origin: An unofficial awareness day tied to environmental and gardening communities, it fits neatly into late spring when many people start their gardens.
holidays.funFact: A healthy compost pile can heat up to 130-160°F (54-71°C) in its center thanks to hardworking microbes, which is hot enough to steam on a cold morning.

holidays.name: International Day of UN Peacekeepers
holidays.description: A day to honor the people who serve in United Nations peacekeeping missions and to remember those who lost their lives in the line of duty.
holidays.origin: The UN General Assembly established it in 2002. May 29 was chosen because it marks the date in 1948 when the first UN peacekeeping mission, the UN Truce Supervision Organization, began operations in the Middle East.
holidays.funFact: UN peacekeepers wear famous light blue helmets and berets, a color chosen because it is seen as neutral and distinct from the colors of military forces.

holidays.name: Paper Clip Day
holidays.description: A tribute to the humble paper clip, the bent-wire office hero that holds your documents together and doubles as a lock pick, phone SIM ejector, and fidget toy.
holidays.origin: An unofficial office-supply and trivia observance. The date is often cited among quirky calendars celebrating everyday inventions.
holidays.funFact: During World War II, Norwegians wore paper clips on their lapels as a quiet symbol of unity and resistance against Nazi occupation.
